problems.problem_text: A bag contains 3 red and 5 blue marbles. One marble is drawn and it is red. It is not replaced. What is the probability that the second marble drawn is also red?
problems.solution: After removing 1 red: 2 red, 5 blue remain. P(second red | first red) = 2/7.

problems.problem_text: A fair dice is rolled. Given that the outcome is an even number, what is the probability that it is a 6?
problems.solution: Even numbers: {2,4,6}. Of these, only 6 is favourable. P(6 | even) = 1/3.

problems.problem_text: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. Given that it is a red card, what is the probability that it is a heart?
problems.solution: Red cards: 26 total (13 hearts + 13 diamonds). Hearts: 13. P(heart | red) = 13/26 = 1/2.

problems.problem_text: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls and 12 are boys. 10 of the girls wear glasses. Given that a student chosen at random is a girl, what is the probability she wears glasses?
problems.solution: Number of girls = 18. Girls who wear glasses = 10. P(glasses | girl) = 10/18 = 5/9.

problems.problem_text: In a survey of 100 students: 60 study French, 40 study German, 25 study both. A student is chosen at random. Given that the student studies French, what is the probability they also study German?
A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that the second marble is red, given that the first marble was blue?
problems.solution: After removing 1 blue: 4 red, 5 blue remain. P(second red | first blue) = 4/9.

problems.problem_text: A fair dice is rolled twice. Given that the sum of the two numbers is 7, what is the probability that the first dice shows a 3?
problems.solution: Ways to sum to 7: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) — 6 equally likely outcomes. Of these, 1 has first dice = 3: (3,4). P = 1/6.

problems.problem_text: A card is drawn from a standard deck. Given that it is a face card (Jack, Queen or King), what is the probability that it is a King?
problems.solution: There are 12 face cards (3 per suit × 4 suits). Kings: 4. P(King | face card) = 4/12 = 1/3.

problems.problem_text:
A two-way table shows:
        Pass   Fail   Total
Boys     28     12     40
Girls    35      5     40
Total    63     17     80
A student is selected at random. Given that the student passed, find the probability that the student is a girl.
problems.solution: Number who passed = 63. Girls who passed = 35. P(girl | passed) = 35/63 = 5/9.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn and it is NOT green. What is the probability that it is red?
problems.solution: Non-green marbles = 5 + 3 = 8. Red marbles among those = 5. P(red | not green) = 5/8.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains 3 red and 7 black balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Given that the balls are of different colours, find the probability that the first ball was red.

The probability that a patient has a disease is 0.02. A test gives a positive result for 95% of people with the disease and for 3% of people without the disease. If a person tests positive, find the probability that they actually have the disease.
A bag contains 4 red and 6 white balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Given that at least one ball is red, find the probability that both balls are red.
A fair dice is rolled. Given that the result is a prime number, find the probability that it is also odd.
problems.solution: Prime numbers on a dice: {2,3,5}. Of these, odd numbers are {3,5}. P(odd | prime) = 2/3.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains 6 red and n white balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. The probability that both balls are red is 1/3. Find n.

A factory has two machines A and B. Machine A produces 60% of the items, machine B produces 40%. Machine A makes 2% defective items, machine B makes 5% defective items. An item is chosen at random and found to be defective. Find the probability that it came from machine A.
